records.title: Architecting efficient context-aware multi-agent framework for production
records.relevance_note: Production-oriented context engineering writeup describing 'context as a compiled view' and handoff translation for multi-agent systems.
records.reason_included: Contains concrete context compilation/working-context assembly metaphors (sessions/memory/artifacts -> compiler pipeline -> working context) and handoff translation mechanics.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The post argues the naive pattern of appending everything into one prompt collapses under cost/latency growth, signal degradation ("lost in the middle"), and eventual window overflow.

It proposes treating context as a compiled view: sessions/memory/artifacts are the sources of structured state, flows/processors are the compiler pipeline, and the working context is the compiled view shipped to the LLM for a single invocation.

For agent handoff, the post describes an active translation: narrative casting of prior assistant messages and explicit attribution/summarisation of tool calls from other agents so the new agent can act on results without misattributing capabilities or history.

records.title: Long-running Claude for scientific computing
records.relevance_note: Explicit topology guidance based on task coupling for long-running scientific coding.
records.reason_included: Provides concrete selection rule for parallel team versus sequential agent plus subagents.

claim_snippets.claim_text: A Boltzmann solver is treated as a deeply coupled pipeline where a single agent working sequentially, spawning subagents as needed, is better suited than a large parallel team.
CLAUDE.md serves as a mutable global plan kept in context, while CHANGELOG.md serves as portable long-term memory so later sessions avoid retrying failed approaches.
A Ralph-loop style orchestration pattern is used to push the agent past premature completion by re-entering context until the explicit success criterion is met.

records.title: Effective harnesses for long-running agents
records.relevance_note: Effective harnesses for long-running agents is a engineering writeup source with details on two role topology, initializer agent relevant to agent architecture.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on topology, memory, artifacts workspace.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The harness uses a two-role topology: an initializer agent creates the initial environment, while a coding agent repeatedly resumes work in later sessions using the artifacts left behind.

The initializer writes init.sh, a progress file, and an initial git commit; later coding sessions read progress notes, git history, and a structured feature list before choosing a single next feature.

The design is explicitly aimed at failure modes where agents try to one-shot the project, leave undocumented half-finished work, or declare victory too early; the proposed mitigation is incremental work plus self-verification before marking features as passing.

records.title: How we built our multi-agent research system
records.exception_reason: Official production architecture writeup for orchestrator-worker research agents; uniquely details delegation rules, memory persistence, and parallelization failures that remain directly relevant to topology design.
records.relevance_note: How we built our multi-agent research system is a engineering writeup source with details on orchestrator worker, parallel subagents relevant to agent architecture.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on topology, execution loop, memory.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The production research system uses an orchestrator-worker topology: a lead agent plans, persists its plan to memory, spawns specialized subagents in parallel, and hands final findings to a CitationAgent.

In Anthropic’s internal research eval, a multi-agent system with Claude Opus 4 lead and Claude Sonnet 4 subagents outperformed single-agent Claude Opus 4 by 90.2%, with token usage explaining most variance on BrowseComp.

Detailed delegation prompts and explicit scaling rules were required to prevent duplicated work and runaway subagent counts; parallelizing both subagents and tool calls cut research time by up to 90%, while synchronous lead-agent execution still created bottlenecks.

records.title: CLAUDE.md startup instructions should be executed, not just loaded as context (Issue #34763)
records.relevance_note: Shows failure mode where startup routines encoded in project policy file are not reliably enforced because they are injected as plain text rather than executed steps.
records.reason_included: Concrete policy failure example (startup routine ignored) with explicit suggestion to treat startup rules as executable pre-steps rather than passive context.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The issue states that CLAUDE.md startup instructions are loaded into the model’s context as text but are not executed as actual steps, so the model can ignore them (especially on simple prompts).
Example startup routine in CLAUDE.md is expressed as an ordered list (read README.md and AGENTS.md, read relevant skills, check agent memory).
In the reproduced conversation, the reporter claims the model answered 'who are you?' with generic identity text rather than following the CLAUDE.md startup routine first.

records.title: Context as a Tool: Context Management for Long-Horizon SWE-Agents
records.relevance_note: Context as a Tool: Context Management for Long-Horizon SWE-Agents is a paper source with details on context as tool, structured context workspace relevant to context engineering.
records.reason_included: Included for source-local evidence on context, memory, eval design.

claim_snippets.claim_text: The paper argues append-only context maintenance or passively triggered compression heuristics can lead to "context explosion, semantic drift, and degraded reasoning" in long-running SWE agent interactions.

CAT formalizes a structured context workspace consisting of "stable task semantics", "condensed long-term memory", and "high-fidelity short-term interactions", and enables agents to proactively compress history into actionable summaries at milestones.
On SWE-Bench-Verified, the paper reports SWE-Compressor reaches a 57.6% solved rate and outperforms ReAct-based agents and static compression baselines under a bounded context budget.

records.title: DyTopo: Dynamic Topology Routing for Multi-Agent Reasoning via Semantic Matching
records.relevance_note: Direct comparison of dynamic versus fixed communication topologies for multi-round agents.
records.reason_included: Contains concrete routing mechanism, memory-update contract, and costed baseline comparisons.

claim_snippets.claim_text: DyTopo reconstructs a sparse directed communication graph every round by semantically matching each agent’s query descriptor to other agents’ key descriptors, then routes only the induced private messages.
Across code-generation and mathematical-reasoning benchmarks with four LLM backbones, DyTopo beats the strongest baseline in all 16 backbone-dataset settings with mean gain about 6.1 points.
Fixed-horizon baselines waste tokens and latency: on HumanEval, DyTopo reaches the highest accuracy while using 48% of AgentScope’s tokens and converging in 2.6 rounds on average.

records.title: Building AI Coding Agents for the Terminal: Scaffolding, Harness, and Lessons Learned
records.relevance_note: Detailed open-source report on agent harness design for terminal.
records.reason_included: Describes planning mode and execution strategies to prevent unsafe operations.

claim_snippets.claim_text: Planning is done by a subagent with read-only tools (no write tools in its schema), eliminating write attempts during planning.
During execution, read-only tools run in parallel (thread pool) and write tools run sequentially.
OPENDEV uses "lazy tool discovery" and "adaptive context compaction" that "progressively reduces older observations" to prevent context bloat during long-horizon terminal work.
OPENDEV employs an "automated memory system" to accumulate project-specific knowledge across sessions and uses "event-driven system reminders" to counteract instruction fade-out.
